question.prompt: \(f(x)=x^2-4x+1\). What is the possible \(x\)-coordinate of a local extremum?

solutions.explanation: \(f'(x)=2x-4=0\), so \(x=2\). The derivative is negative to the left and positive to the right, so this is a local minimum point.
solutions.title: Derivative sign test

solutions.explanation:
Completing the square exposes the vertex:
\[
f(x)=x^2-4x+1=(x-2)^2-3.
\]
For every real \(x\), \((x-2)^2\ge0\), with equality only at \(x=2\). Hence the vertex \((2,-3)\) is a minimum point and therefore also a local minimum point. The requested \(x\)-coordinate is \(2\).
solutions.title: Completing the square
